cards.text: Friend, we left Joseph on his way to Egypt, and now he's there. An Egyptian named Potiphar buys him from the Ishmaelites who took him there. Potiphar is an officer of Pharaoh, Egypt's king.

cards.question: Potiphar isn't just any officer of Pharaoh. What's his job?

cards.text: So Joseph is serving in the household of his Egyptian master, a long way from home. But he is NOT alone in that house.

cards.question: Joseph becomes a successful man in Potiphar's household. Who does the text say is with him?
True or false: Potiphar can see that the LORD is with Joseph and makes him prosper in all he does.

cards.text: Joseph finds favor with Potiphar and becomes his personal attendant. From the new guy to the boss's right-hand man, friend, that's a PROMOTION.

cards.question: Potiphar puts Joseph in charge of his ___ and entrusts him with everything he owns.

cards.text: From the moment Joseph takes charge, something changes in that house. And it's all on account of Joseph.

cards.question: What does the LORD do for Potiphar's household on account of Joseph?

answers.text: He makes Potiphar's enemies fear him

cards.question: True or false: The LORD's blessing reaches Potiphar's house but stops at his field.

cards.text: Potiphar leaves all he owns in Joseph's care and stops concerning himself with any of it. Well. Almost any of it.

cards.question: With Joseph running everything, what's the one thing Potiphar still concerns himself with?

cards.text: Now Joseph is well-built and handsome. After some time, Potiphar's wife casts her eyes on him and says, “Sleep with me.”

cards.question: Joseph refuses and reminds her how much his master trusts him. What has Potiphar withheld from Joseph?
True or false: Joseph tells Potiphar's wife that no one in the house is greater than he is.
Joseph ends his answer with a question. What does he call doing what Potiphar's wife asks?

answers.text: A great evil and a sin against God
A great shame and a disgrace before Egypt
A great folly and a dishonor to his father

cards.text: Day after day she keeps speaking to him, and day after day Joseph refuses. Friend, I can't say no to ONE warm cookie, and this man is saying no EVERY DAY.

cards.question: Joseph won't go to bed with Potiphar's wife. How far does he go to keep his distance?

answers.text: He won't even be near her
He only works when Potiphar is home
He asks to be sent to the fields

cards.text: Then one day, Joseph goes into the house to do his work. Not a single household servant is inside.

cards.question: Potiphar's wife grabs Joseph by his cloak and says it again. What does Joseph do?

answers.text: Leaves the cloak and runs outside
Pulls free and calls for the servants
Stays and tells her no once more

cards.text: She sees the cloak in her hand and Joseph out of the house. So she calls in her household servants.

cards.question: What does Potiphar's wife tell the household servants?

answers.text: That Joseph came to her and she screamed
That Joseph stole a cloak from Potiphar
That Joseph ran away from his work

cards.question: True or false: In her story, Joseph heard her scream and left his cloak beside her.

cards.text: That's not what happened, and we both know it. She keeps Joseph's cloak beside her until his master comes home.

cards.question: True or false: When Potiphar gets home, his wife tells him a different story than she told the servants.

cards.text: Potiphar hears it all. His wife tells him this is what his slave did to her.

cards.question: How does Potiphar react to his wife's story?

answers.text: He asks the servants what they saw
He sends for Joseph to explain

cards.question: What does Potiphar do with Joseph?

answers.text: Has him thrown into the king's prison
Sends him to work in the fields

cards.text: Friend, I know that move: one day you're on the counter, and the next you're in the back of a junk drawer next to a dead battery. But while Joseph is there in the prison, that line again: the LORD was with him.

cards.question: In prison, the LORD extends kindness to Joseph. How?

answers.text: He grants him favor with the warden
He opens the prison doors at night
He makes Potiphar regret his anger

cards.question: The prison warden puts all the ___ under Joseph's care.

cards.text: So now Joseph is responsible for all that's done in the prison. In the house, IN CHARGE, in the prison, IN CHARGE, and I bet if you dropped him in my old junk drawer he'd have the rubber bands lined up by the end of the day.

cards.question: True or false: The prison warden keeps a close eye on everything under Joseph's care.

cards.text: The LORD gives Joseph success in whatever he does, even in a prison. But friend, he's still sitting behind those walls, and this story has a LOT more to go.

findings.problem: The card says 'we left Joseph on his way to Egypt.' But the last passage in the Joseph group ends at Genesis 37:36, which says the Midianites had already sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar. He wasn't still on his way. The card should start from where the last passage actually left him.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'Who does the text say is with him?' sounds like a test question, not Papa Dorin pausing mid-story. Card 3 just set it up with 'he is NOT alone in that house,' so the question should come out of that moment, for example 'So who's with him?'

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: This is a which-thing question. One wrong answer, 'Nothing except his storehouse keys,' isn't a real detail from the Bible. The other wrong answer, the signet ring, is fine: it's real (Genesis 41:42). Replace the storehouse keys with a real biblical item.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: From card 1 through card 10, stop 2 has no humor at all. That covers the empty house, the cloak, the story she tells and Potiphar's anger. The story cards there (1, 3, 6, 8) just report what happens. A moment like Joseph running out and leaving his cloak in her hand could hold a real laugh, kept to Joseph's human situation and not to the sin, without muddying any fact.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
